title: TTL-graft session handshake for regional cutover
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight TTL-graft handshake protocol to enable gradual, low-latency regional cutovers for active-active hosted API gateways while preserving streaming session continuity and respecting SLOs. This ticket designs and ships a gateway-side flow that: 1) establishes an ephemeral graft token (short TTL) and associated KV lease, 2) performs a controlled traffic taper from primary-region pods to target-region pods, and 3) uses a handshake to transfer minimal session state (router offsets, streaming cursor, small prefix cache pointers) to allow resumed streams without full replay. The protocol must integrate with existing circuit breakers and load-shedding policies so we avoid amplifying overloaded regions during cutover.
acceptance_criteria:
- Handshake protocol implemented and enabled behind feature flag in staging.
- End-to-end streaming resume for >95% of sessions after cutover without user-visible duplication or loss under normal SLO load.
- 99th-percentile additional latency introduced by handshake < 30ms on median regional link.
- Graceful degradation path: when graft fails, fallback switches to existing hard-cutover flow with documented error codes and automated rollback.
- Unit/integration tests + chaos test run added to CI.
- Monitoring dashboards for graft success rate, graft latency, abort reasons, and traffic taper progression live in Console.
implementation_notes:
High-level plan: (1) Controller component will coordinate graft windows and compute taper schedule per-market. (2) Gateway edge implements GRAFT_PREPARE, GRAFT_COMMIT, GRAFT_ABORT messages over control plane with small signed token. GRAFT_PREPARE reserves an ephemeral KV lease containing pointers to the prefix/KV cache and a short-lived transfer token. (3) Traffic taper implemented as weighted egress adjustment with exponential decay (configurable halflife). (4) For streaming sessions, we transfer mime-type, last-ack-offset, active tool calls snapshot (opaque small blob), and a pointer to prefix cache entries; target region validates token and pulls necessary cached items lazily. (5) Circuit breaker integration: graft operations respect per-region SLO headroom; controller will abort or slow taper if region headroom < threshold. (6) Load-shedding: if target region triggers shedding during graft, we surface a GRAFT_ABORT with structured reason and trigger fallback drain.
Key implementation constraints: minimize synchronous cross-region fetches; prefer pointer-based lazy fetches to avoid added tail latency. Use existing KV cache replication hooks where possible. Ensure tokens are short-lived (e.g., 10s) and cryptographically signed; audit logs emitted for each graft action.

risks_mitigation:
Risk: Cross-region KV fetchs during resume could add high tail latency. Mitigation: use pointer + lazy fetch strategy; prewarm small prefix cache for top N customers.
Risk: Aborted grafts leave half-open sessions. Mitigation: ensure GRAFT_ABORT triggers immediate affinity revert and emit metrics; add compensating cleanup job to expire orphaned leases.
Risk: Malformed tokens or replay attacks. Mitigation: sign tokens with rotating KMS key, include nonce and short TTL; require audit logging.
Risk: Overloading target region during aggressive taper. Mitigation: controller computes taper plan using current capacity headroom and SLO buffers; integrate with autoscaler and circuit-breakers to slow or pause taper.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token lifecycle and signature verification.
- Integration tests: end-to-end graft prepare/commit/abort flows with simulated network partition.
- Streaming harness: replay user traffic in staging and trigger regional cutover; assert resume correctness and observe token/pointer lazy fetch behavior.
- Chaos/Failure tests: inject target region shedding and ensure fallback path engaged and no data duplication.
- Load tests: synthetic customers at 10x baseline to validate taper safety and circuit-breaker interactions.
- SLO verification: run 24h soak with graft enabled and verify SLOs (p50/p95/p99 for latency, success rate for resumes).
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal staging): feature-flagged rollout to canary edge nodes for internal traffic only.
Phase 1 (low-risk customers): enable for <5% traffic in a single non-critical region. Monitor graft success rate and graft latency metrics for 48h.
Phase 2 (regional ramp): gradual ramp to target region with automated taper policy; enable circuit-breaker thresholds for automatic abort.
Phase 3 (global): enable for multi-region active-active flows and reduce monitoring thresholds.
Rollback criteria: >2% severe resume failures or >5% increase in 99p tail latency attributed to graft actions for >30m => automated abort and full rollback.
